observation.visible_scene: Close-up of a supine patient's face (eyes closed) during an oral/maxillofacial procedure. The mouth is held open; the upper lip/cheek is retracted by a metal cheek-retractor loop, a blue endotracheal tube and a small blue printed balloon tag sit at the right side of the mouth, and teal and blue surgical drapes frame the face. A gloved right hand at the upper-right holds a long flat metal blade angled toward the mouth. A gloved left hand works at the lower jaw, its index finger pulling the lower lip outward while holding a second flat metal blade against the lower teeth.
visible_changes: The large out-of-focus foreground mass (the left gloved hand/instrument held very near the lens) in frame 1 moves up and away by frames 2-3, bringing the left hand and its flat blade into focus at the left of the face.

The left hand's flat blade transitions from a vertical, blurred orientation (frames 2-4) to an angled position with its tip seated at the lower incisors/lower lip (frames 5-8 onward), where it remains with only small angular and depth adjustments through the last frame.
The left index finger maintains and slightly varies its retraction of the lower lip, exposing the lower teeth.
The right hand and its diagonal flat blade, the upper cheek retractor, the blue tube and tag, and the patient's closed eyes and open mouth remain essentially static throughout.
The framing appears to widen slightly as the foreground obstruction clears, revealing more of the forehead and both brows.
outside_clip_unknowns: The purpose or name of the flat blades (retraction vs. cutting/osteotomy) and the overall procedure.
What happens before frame 1 and after frame 41.
The exact identity of the instruments and the patient's condition.
uncertain_details: Whether the apparent framing change is camera motion (slight zoom/pan) or simply the foreground hand moving out of the optical path.
The precise mechanical action of the left blade against the lower teeth (prying, retracting, or stabilizing) cannot be confirmed from the stills alone.
